summary: Intro discovery for Redwood PLG quickstart. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for initial integration. Interested in fast time-to-first-token, free credits for evaluation, and security compliance (SOC2, KMS). Follow-ups: quickstart guide, security pack, and technical benchmark session.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jamie from Redwood, this is Luis our SE. Quick intro?
[00:09] Aisha Khan: Hi I'm Aisha, CTO at Sequoia Ventures, we've got Ben and Maya on the call.
[00:14] Ben Park: Hey all.
[00:17] Luis Martinez: Great, thanks. Agenda — quick discovery, show how the quickstart works, answer security q's, agree next steps.
[00:30] Aisha: We're primarily exploring embedding and chat features for our support bot and a few internal analytics tasks. Main goals are speed to integrate and keeping costs under control.
[00:45] Ben: Tech stack — we're on GCP, k8s for infra, some on-prem data lake. Right now using ProviderX for embeddings and OpenAI for generation in a couple prototypes.
[01:05] Luis: Nice, Redwood has a self-serve API for hosted mode — you can get free credits, quickstart SDKs, and get to a token in minutes. If you need consistent throughput there's Dedicated, and for strict compliance we offer Private (VPC/on-prem).
[01:27] Maya: Security is big for us. We need SOC 2, audit logs, KMS integration, and SSO/SAML. Also curious about data residency.
[01:40] Jamie: Absolutely, we support SSO, audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations — we'll share the security pack after this call.
[01:50] Aisha: Timeline — if it takes too long to spin up we'll move on. We want to run a POC in ~2–3 weeks if possible.
[02:01] Ben: Also latency matters for the support bot; sub-200ms token latency would be ideal, but cost matters too.
[02:12] Luis: Good note. Tradeoffs: hosted is fastest to start and easiest to manage, Dedicated gives predictable latency/cost at scale, Private gives control for regulatory needs. For protos, hosted + caching is usually best.
[02:36] Aisha: How quick is the quickstart? We saw "time-to-first-token" claims on the site.
[02:42] Jamie: Typical is under 15 minutes for a dev to get keys, run the SDK example, and receive the first streaming token. We'll provide a sample notebook that does embeddings and a small chat flow.
[02:58] Ben: Does the hosted API allow prefix/KV caching or do we handle that?
[03:05] Luis: We handle prefix and KV caching at the runtime level for hosted and Dedicated. For Private, caching config is available but managed by the customer's infra.
[03:20] Maya: Any limitations on model choices in hosted vs dedicated?
[03:25] Jamie: Hosted has our curated open models plus Redwood-verified performance profiles. Dedicated lets you pin models and variants; Private supports the same but needs approval for some proprietary kernels. Sometimes names in transcripts look off — we call out e.g., KV cache or K V cache — sorry for the speech stuff.
[03:45] Ben: For cost projection, are there calculators?
[03:48] Luis: Yes, we have a cost estimator and Optimize tool that suggests batching/quantization. We'll share a spreadsheet and examples.
[04:05] Aisha: On the security front — can you confirm data retention and deletion options?
[04:12] Jamie: Hosted: configurable retention, enterprise tenants can opt-out of retention. Dedicated: no co-mingling and configurable retention. Private: you control retention entirely. We'll send the exact policy.
[04:30] Ben: Who owns the keys in hosted?
[04:34] Luis: Hosted offers optional customer-managed keys via KMS; otherwise Redwood-managed keys.
[04:40] Maya: We need SSO and RBAC for multiple teams.
[04:44] Jamie: Supported — we have role-based controls in the Console and SAML/SSO integrations.
[04:52] Aisha: For the POC, what would success look like?
[04:56] Ben: 1) integrate embeddings into search with improved recall, 2) chat responses under 300ms median, 3) cost within our forecast.
[05:10] Luis: Good measurable goals. We'll help design the benchmark with sample prompts.
[05:20] Aisha: Any blockers with our on-prem data? We need private connect for sensitive stuff.
[05:27] Jamie: For sensitive data, Private or a VPC Dedicated option is typical. For quick POC, bring a de-identified subset to hosted to validate models, then shift to Dedicated/Private for production.
[05:45] Ben: How do rollouts work? Canary or A/B?
[05:48] Luis: Both. Console supports canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants.
[06:00] Maya: About compliance docs — we need SOC2 Type II and penetration test reports.
[06:06] Jamie: We'll include SOC2, ISO certs, pen-test summary in the security pack.
[06:12] Ben: Pricing — do you do free credits for evaluation?
[06:16] Jamie: Yes, we provide evaluation credits tied to your account for PLG quickstarts. Amount depends on scope; we usually give enough for 2–3 weeks of testing for the POC.
[06:28] Aisha: Any hidden costs like tail usage or long-term storage charges?
[06:33] Luis: We'll be transparent; tokens and embeddings are billed, optional storage and advanced observability are add-ons. We'll send a sample pricing sheet.
[06:45] Ben: On benchmarks — can Redwood run a baseline with our sample prompts?
[06:49] Luis: We can run a lightweight benchmark; for deeper perf we'll schedule a dedicated session and can test on Dedicated if you want.
[06:58] Aisha: If we decide to go Dedicated later, how disruptive is migration?
[07:03] Jamie: Minimal — same API, just change routing and provisioning. We support model pinning so rollouts are smooth.
[07:12] Ben: Any SLA on Dedicated?
[07:15] Luis: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include SLA details in follow-ups.
[07:24] Maya: For private deployments, what's the ops footprint?
[07:28] Jamie: Private is heavier — you run control plane or we provide a customer-managed control plane, there are on-prem packages; we'll include deployment guides.
[07:38] Aisha: We have a couple of stakeholders from legal and infra who might join next call.
[07:42] Jamie: Great — we'll invite them for the security deep dive.
[07:50] Ben: Any gotchas with our GCP k8s environment?
[07:54] Luis: Mostly networking/VPC peering and IAM; we have guides for k8s sidecars and GPU provisioning if you plan local inference.
[08:05] Aisha: What's the expected token latency in hosted for smaller models?
[08:10] Luis: For curated open models on hosted, median per-token latencies can be ~20–60ms depending on sequence length and batching. For end-to-end response time it depends on prompt size and streaming.
[08:26] Ben: Do you support function/tool calling and structured output?
[08:30] Jamie: Yes, streaming responses, function calling, and structured outputs are supported in API.
[08:36] Maya: About audit logs — are they immutable and exportable?
[08:40] Luis: Yes, audit logs are exportable to your SIEM and can be set up for long-term retention.
[08:48] Aisha: Can you walk through a quick demo of the quickstart flow?
[08:52] Luis: Sure I'll do a high-level — create account, get API key, pip install redwood-sdk, run the sample notebook. You'll see embeddings creation, a quick reranker, and a chat sample streaming tokens.
[09:08] Ben: Does the notebook include code for re-ranking with embeddings?
[09:12] Luis: Yes, sample snippet uses embeddings endpoint and a small ranker.
[09:18] Aisha: How are rate limits handled for evaluation?
[09:22] Jamie: We can set temporary higher quotas for the POC.
[09:26] Maya: Any mis-transcriptions in the call — weird names? Nothing from me.
[09:32] Jamie: (laughter) Yeah Fireflies sometimes messes up product names.
[09:36] Ben: Quick question — what monitoring is available out-of-the-box?
[09:40] Luis: Console has per-route token cost, latency, request tracing, and anomaly alerts. You can also export traces.
[09:50] Aisha: Ok let's align on next steps and owners.
[09:54] Jamie: I'll send quickstart guide, sample notebook, security pack, and pricing. Luis will coordinate a technical deep dive and baseline run. Maya will send security checklist.
[10:08] Aisha: Sounds good.
[10:10] Ben: Appreciate the clarity, excited to try quickstart.
[10:14] Maya: Thanks.
[10:18] Jamie: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links and invites.
[44:30] [call ends]
